Computational analysis via DharmaNexus indicates extensive Pali-internal text reuse, recording 452 matches across 28 Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. The largest share of textual alignment occurs with its commentary, the *Buddhavaṁsa-aṭṭhakathā* (172 matches; e.g., segments §23.1–32.4), as well as the *Apadāna-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. In addition, repetitive biographical verse structures share substantial material with other chapters of the *Buddhavaṁsa*, including the *Sumanabuddhavaṁsa* (Bv 6; segments §14.4–21.2), *Padumuttarabuddhavaṁsa* (Bv 12), and *Piyadassībuddhavaṁsa* (Bv 15) [DharmaNexus]. Beyond Pali, DharmaNexus automatically aligns passages of the text with Tibetan works, yielding notable matches with the Tibetan translation of the *Jātakanidāna* (D0032) and lower-scoring alignments with the *Ārya-avalokana-nāma-mahāyāna-sūtra* (D0195) [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on catalog and DharmaNexus data.*
